response: {"title":"Minimal failing-input shrink","intervention":"For each newly observed boundary or invalid-input failure, shrink the input to the smallest value that preserves the failure, then make the fix satisfy both that minimal case and its nearest valid neighbor with the exact expected return or exception class and message.","claim":"Against no appended instruction, minimal failing-input shrinkage will improve held-out edge-semantics pass_rate on matched Python tasks within the same deadline, while wall_time and turns reveal its cost.","mechanism":"Shrinking removes irrelevant input features, isolates the responsible predicate, and pairs it with the adjacent accepted case, reducing overbroad patches and incorrect error normalization.","assumptions":["At least one failing example is available from tests or direct probing.","Inputs can be simplified manually within the deadline.","A meaningful valid neighbor and exact expected behavior can be inferred."],"risks":["Manual shrinking may consume time or stop at a non-minimal case.","The smallest failure may not represent interaction-heavy hidden cases.","Some domains lack an obvious size ordering or valid neighbor.","Fixing the minimal case can overfit if the underlying contract is misunderstood."],"test_plan":{"experiment":"Randomize matched multi-module Python repair tasks between this appended instruction and no appended instruction with identical models, tools, failing examples, and deadlines; evaluate hidden boundary, invalid-input, exception-class, and exact-message tests.","metrics":["pass_rate","wall_time","turns"],"success_condition":"The intervention arm has higher hidden pass_rate overall and on nearest-neighbor edge cases, remains within the fixed deadline, and does not materially increase median turns."},"single_shot_ordinal":10}
